title: A Phase II Study of HS-10561 Capsules in Adults With Chronic Primary Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP)
off: A Phase II Study of HS-10561 Capsules in Adults With Chronic Primary Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP)
summary: This is a multicenter, open-label, randomized, parallel-group Phase II clinical trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of HS-10561 capsules in adult participants with chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP).
desc:
Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an acquired, organ-specific autoimmune disorder characterized by a decreased platelet count and by mucocutaneous bleeding. Despite the availability of several treatment options, response to therapy is frequently unsatisfactory, and a substantial proportion of patients require long-term maintenance treatment.

Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) plays a key role in B-cell development, activation and autoantibody production. This mechanism is of considerable importance in the pathogenesis of autoimmune diseases such as ITP and provides a rationale for BTK inhibition as a therapeutic strategy that addresses both the autoantibody-producing B-cell compartment and the antibody-dependent clearance of platelets by the reticuloendothelial system.

HS-10561 is an orally administered small-molecule BTK inhibitor with potent BTK inhibitory activity. Nonclinical studies and Phase I clinical study data support the clinical development of HS-10561 in ITP.

This study is a multicenter, open-label, randomized, parallel-group Phase II clinical trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of different doses of HS-10561 capsules in adult participants with chronic ITP who have received at least one prior standard first-line ITP therapy (corticosteroids and/or intravenous immunoglobulin) and achieved a platelet count ≥50×10\^9/L but whose response could not be maintained or who subsequently relapsed. The study consists of a Screening Period (4 weeks), a Treatment Period (24 weeks), an Extension Treatment Period \[28 weeks (optional)\] and a Safety Follow-up Period (4 weeks). Approximately 60 participants who meet the protocol eligibility criteria will be enrolled and randomized 1:1, stratified by baseline platelet count (defined as the platelet count measured within 24 hours before randomization) (\<15×10\^9/L vs ≥15×10\^9/L), to receive HS-10561 15mg QD or 30mg QD. All participants will receive continuous oral HS-10561 until intolerance or for 24 weeks with periodic efficacy and safety assessments. Participants who have completed 24 weeks of study treatment and, in the investigator's judgment, may benefit from continuing the current treatment may, on a voluntary basis, enter the Extension Treatment Period and continue the current dose for up to 52 weeks. After the end of study treatment, participants will enter the Safety Follow-up Period (4 weeks after the last dose) or until initiation of a new ITP treatment, whichever occurs first. Efficacy will be assessed by platelet count, the World Health Organization (WHO) bleeding score and the receipt of emergency treatment aimed at increasing platelet count; safety will be assessed by adverse events, laboratory tests, vital signs and 12-lead electrocardiogram; and the effect of HS-10561 on quality of life will be explored using ITP-PAQ scores.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Subjects comprehensively understand and can adhere to the study protocol requirements and willingly signed the informed consent form.
* Age 18 to 80 years, inclusive; male or female.
* Diagnosis of primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) according to the 2019 International Working Group (IWG) consensus criteria, with a duration of ITP of more than 12 months.
* History of at least one prior standard first-line ITP therapy (corticosteroids and/or IVIg) after which the response could not be maintained, or relapse.
* Documented history of response to prior standard ITP therapy (i.e., a platelet count ≥50×10\^9/L has previously been achieved).
* Mean platelet count \<30×10\^9/L based on at least 2 measurements performed during the Screening Period at least 5 days apart, with each individual value ≤35×10\^9/L.
* No major bleeding within 4 weeks before randomization, i.e., a World Health Organization (WHO) bleeding score of 0 to 2.
* Receipt of concomitant corticosteroids (prednisone-equivalent dose ≤20 mg/day) and/or a thrombopoietin receptor agonist (TPO-RA) at a stable dose (no more than a 10% change in dose within 2 weeks before randomization) is permitted during the study.
* ECOG performance status of 0 to 2.
* Fertile female and male patients must use effective contraception separately during the study and for 3 months after the cessation of study drug treatment.
* For fertile female patients, a negative pregnancy test result is required.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Evidence of all kinds of secondary thrombocytopenia or autoimmune hemolytic anemia.
* History of another primary malignancy.
* History of coagulation disorders other than ITP.
* Prior bone marrow/hematopoietic stem cell transplantation or major solid organ transplantation.
* Requirement for long-term/continuous treatment with products that affect platelet function or with anticoagulants.
* Prior or current treatment with ITP-directed therapies.
* Inadequate bone marrow reserve or hepatic or renal function.
* Severe cardiac criteria in: QTcF \>470 msec; significant ECG abnormality; QT/arrhythmia risk factors; NYHA III-IV heart failure.
* Severe, uncontrolled, or active cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease.
* Severe or poorly controlled diabetes mellitus.
* Severe or poorly controlled hypertension.
* Active hepatitis B.
* Active hepatitis C, HIV infection, or active CMV infection.
* Active tuberculosis.
* History of intracranial hemorrhage or other severe bleeding in vital organs, or symptomatic gastrointestinal bleeding.
* Major surgery within 4 weeks before randomization.
* Severe infection within 4 weeks before randomization.
* A live attenuated vaccine within 8 weeks before randomization.
* Severe arterial or venous thrombotic events.
* Prior treatment with a BTK inhibitor.
* Use of strong inducers or strong inhibitors of CYP3A4 within 2 weeks or 5 half-lives.
* Clinically significant gastrointestinal abnormalities that may affect drug intake, transit, or absorption.
* Hepatic encephalopathy, hepatorenal syndrome, or cirrhosis of ≥Child-Pugh class B.
* History of severe neurological or psychiatric disorders.
* Women who are pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study.
* History of severe allergic reactions.
* Any condition that, in the investigator's judgment, would jeopardize the safety of the participant or interfere with study assessments.

primary.m: Proportion of participants achieving a durable platelet response
primary.tf: Weeks 13 to 24 of the Treatment Period (6 scheduled visits per participant)

x.titre: HS-10561, inhibiteur de BTK, à deux doses dans le PTI chronique de l'adulte
x.question: Le HS-10561, inhibiteur oral de BTK, à 15 mg ou 30 mg par jour est-il efficace et sûr chez l'adulte atteint de PTI chronique ?
x.contexte:
Le purpura thrombopénique immunologique (PTI) est une maladie auto-immune acquise caractérisée par une thrombopénie et un syndrome hémorragique cutanéo-muqueux. Malgré plusieurs options thérapeutiques, la réponse est souvent insuffisante et beaucoup de patients nécessitent un traitement d'entretien prolongé.

La tyrosine kinase de Bruton (BTK) joue un rôle clé dans l'activation des lymphocytes B et la production d'autoanticorps, ainsi que dans la phagocytose des plaquettes opsonisées par les macrophages. Son inhibition cible donc deux mécanismes de la maladie. Le rilzabrutinib est un inhibiteur de BTK qui a déjà montré des résultats dans le PTI.

Le HS-10561 est un inhibiteur de BTK oral développé par Jiangsu Hansoh Pharmaceutical. Les études précliniques et une étude de phase 1 en soutiennent le développement dans le PTI.

Cet essai de phase 2 multicentrique, randomisé et ouvert, prévoit d'inclure environ 60 adultes atteints de PTI chronique ayant déjà répondu à un traitement de première ligne sans maintenir la réponse. Ils reçoivent 15 mg ou 30 mg par jour pendant 24 semaines, avec une extension optionnelle jusqu'à 52 semaines. L'efficacité est suivie par la numération plaquettaire, le score hémorragique de l'OMS et le recours à un traitement de secours.
x.interet: Il pourrait établir la dose et le signal d'efficacité du HS-10561 dans le PTI, et ajouter un inhibiteur de BTK oral à l'arsenal des traitements d'entretien.
